cond_0001.intro: This position requires a proficient and experienced Sr. Research Specialist to work in a busy immunology core facility specializing in flow cytometry, cell sorting, and multiplex biomarker assays using Luminex and ELISA. Experience in flow cytometry is desired but not required. After initial training, the successful candidate will work independently or with minimal supervision. Applicants must demonstrate attention to detail, as well as good communication and critical thinking skills. Organization, efficiency, problem solving skills, resourcefulness, and flexibility are required for this position.
cond_0001.responsibilities: Preparation of samples for flow cytometric assays. Support research projects including thawing cryopreserved cells, staining cells with fluorescently labelled antibodies and flow cytometry sample acquisition. Data interpretation, analysis, and data entry. Train students, staff, and faculty to operate flow cytometers. Assist core facility users with flow cytometry experimental design, optimization, and troubleshooting. Discussion of testing results with laboratory manager, laboratory director, and core facility users. Analysis of data, formulation of conclusions, and creation of appropriate statistical presentations, including graphs and charts, for the purpose of reporting research/laboratory results. Using various software applications, such as Microsoft Office, GraphPad Prism, FlowJo and other flow cytometry software programs to analyze, format and present data and/or test reports. Excellent organizational and time management skills required. Independent and self-motivated, requiring limited supervision once trained. Highly organized and detail oriented. Ability to manage multiple and competing priorities required. Excellent oral and written communication skills required. Demonstrated strong, positive interpersonal skills. Ability to communicate effectively and work in a collaborative team environment. Maintenance of laboratory supplies and laboratory equipment. Preparation of standard laboratory solutions, media, and reagents following standard laboratory protocols and procedures. Rigorous use of universal safety precautions to protect self and co-workers from biohazardous materials, including blood-borne pathogens. Compliance with biohazard safety standards through proper handling of potentially hazardous chemical and biological agents in the workplace. Completion of annual university safety training, as appropriate. Applicant should have laboratory experience to include basic laboratory skills and experience working with biological samples. Perform reasonable job duties even if not part of the job description, as assigned by the Principal Investigator or laboratory supervisor.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's Degree in Biology, Chemistry or related field.
Four years experience in a comparable laboratory performing relevant techniques.
Preferred Requirements
Master's Degree, with related graduate research, may substitute for experience to the extent permitted by the equivalency formula.
Experience running flow cytometers and/or setting up flow cytometry assays.
Applicants who do not meet the posted requirements but are completing their final academic semester/quarter will be considered eligible for employment and may be asked to provide additional information confirming their academic completion date.

Applicants must demonstrate attention to detail, as well as good communication and critical thinking skills. Organization, efficiency, problem solving skills, resourcefulness, and flexibility are required for this position.
cond_0021.responsibilities: Preparation of samples for flow cytometric assays. Support research projects including thawing cryopreserved cells, staining cells with fluorescently labelled antibodies and flow cytometry sample acquisition. Data interpretation, analysis, and data entry. Train students, staff, and faculty to operate flow cytometers. Assist core facility users with flow cytometry experimental design, optimization, and troubleshooting. Discussion of testing results with laboratory manager, laboratory director, and core facility users. Analysis of data, formulation of conclusions, and creation of appropriate statistical presentations, including graphs and charts, for the purpose of reporting research/laboratory results. Using various software applications, such as Microsoft Office, GraphPad Prism, FlowJo and other flow cytometry software programs to analyze, format and present data and/or test reports. Excellent organizational and time management skills required. Independent and self-motivated, requiring limited supervision once trained. Highly organized and detail oriented. Ability to manage multiple and competing priorities required. Excellent oral and written communication skills required. Demonstrated strong, positive interpersonal skills. Ability to communicate effectively and work in a collaborative team environment. Maintenance of laboratory supplies and laboratory equipment. Preparation of standard laboratory solutions, media, and reagents following standard laboratory protocols and procedures. Rigorous use of universal safety precautions to protect self and co-workers from biohazardous materials, including blood-borne pathogens. Compliance with biohazard safety standards through proper handling of potentially hazardous chemical and biological agents in the workplace. Completion of annual university safety training, as appropriate. Applicant should have laboratory experience to include basic laboratory skills and experience working with biological samples. Perform reasonable job duties even if not part of the job description, as assigned by the Principal Investigator or laboratory supervisor.
cond_0021.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Biology, Chemistry, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Around four years of experience in a comparable laboratory performing relevant techniques, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Familiarity with basic laboratory skills and experience working with biological samples.
Preferred Requirements
Experience running flow cytometers and/or setting up flow cytometry assays.
Master's degree with related graduate research (may substitute for experience to the extent permitted by the equivalency formula).
Applicants who do not yet meet the posted requirements but are completing their final academic semester/quarter will be considered eligible for employment and may be asked to provide additional information confirming their academic completion date.

Ability to manage multiple and competing priorities required. Excellent oral and written communication skills required. Demonstrated strong, positive interpersonal skills. Preparation of standard laboratory solutions, media, and reagents following standard laboratory protocols and procedures. Rigorous use of universal safety precautions to protect self and co-workers from biohazardous materials, including blood-borne pathogens. Compliance with biohazard safety standards through proper handling of potentially hazardous chemical and biological agents in the workplace. cond_0147.intro: This position is for a Sr. Research Specialist to work in a busy immunology core facility specializing in flow cytometry, cell sorting, and multiplex biomarker assays using Luminex and ELISA. Experience in flow cytometry is desired but not required. After initial training, the successful candidate will work independently or with minimal supervision. Applicants must demonstrate attention to detail, as well as good communication and critical thinking skills. Organization, efficiency, problem solving skills, resourcefulness, and flexibility are required for this position.
cond_0147.responsibilities: Preparation of samples for flow cytometric assays. Support research projects including thawing cryopreserved cells, staining cells with fluorescently labelled antibodies and flow cytometry sample acquisition. Data interpretation, analysis, and data entry. Train students, staff, and faculty to operate flow cytometers. Assist core facility users with flow cytometry experimental design, optimization, and troubleshooting. Discussion of testing results with laboratory manager, laboratory director, and core facility users. Analysis of data, formulation of conclusions, and creation of appropriate statistical presentations, including graphs and charts, for the purpose of reporting research/laboratory results. Using various software applications, such as Microsoft Office, GraphPad Prism, FlowJo and other flow cytometry software programs to analyze, format and present data and/or test reports. Excellent organizational and time management skills required. Independent and self-motivated, requiring limited supervision once trained. Highly organized and detail oriented. Ability to manage multiple and competing priorities required. Excellent oral and written communication skills required. Demonstrated strong, positive interpersonal skills. Ability to communicate effectively and work in a collaborative team environment. Maintenance of laboratory supplies and laboratory equipment. Preparation of standard laboratory solutions, media, and reagents following standard laboratory protocols and procedures. Rigorous use of universal safety precautions to protect self and co-workers from biohazardous materials, including blood-borne pathogens. Compliance with biohazard safety standards through proper handling of potentially hazardous chemical and biological agents in the workplace. Completion of annual university safety training, as appropriate. Applicant should have laboratory experience to include basic laboratory skills and experience working with biological samples. Perform reasonable job duties even if not part of the job description, as assigned by the Principal Investigator or laboratory supervisor.
cond_0147.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Biology, Chemistry, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Around four years of experience in a comparable laboratory performing relevant techniques, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Familiarity with basic laboratory skills and experience working with biological samples.
Preferred Requirements
Experience running flow cytometers and/or setting up flow cytometry assays.
Master's degree with related graduate research (may substitute for experience to the extent permitted by the equivalency formula).
Applicants who do not yet meet the posted requirements but are completing their final academic semester/quarter will be considered eligible for employment and may be asked to provide additional information confirming their academic completion date.

Experience in flow cytometry is desired but not required. After initial training, the successful candidate will work independently or with minimal supervision. Applicants must demonstrate attention to detail, as well as good communication and critical thinking skills. Organization, efficiency, problem solving skills, resourcefulness, and flexibility are required for this position.
cond_0254.responsibilities: Preparation of samples for flow cytometric assays. Data interpretation, analysis, and data entry. Train students, staff, and faculty to operate flow cytometers. Assist core facility users with flow cytometry experimental design, optimization, and troubleshooting. Discussion of testing results with laboratory manager, laboratory director, and core facility users. Analysis of data, formulation of conclusions, and creation of appropriate statistical presentations, including graphs and charts, for the purpose of reporting research/laboratory results. Using various software applications, such as Microsoft Office, GraphPad Prism, FlowJo and other flow cytometry software programs to analyze, format and present data and/or test reports. Excellent organizational and time management skills required. Independent and self-motivated, requiring limited supervision once trained. Highly organized and detail oriented. Ability to manage multiple and competing priorities required. Excellent oral and written communication skills required. Demonstrated strong, positive interpersonal skills. Ability to communicate effectively and work in a collaborative team environment. Maintenance of laboratory supplies and laboratory equipment. Preparation of standard laboratory solutions, media, and reagents following standard laboratory protocols and procedures. Rigorous use of universal safety precautions to protect self and co-workers from biohazardous materials, including blood-borne pathogens. Compliance with biohazard safety standards through proper handling of potentially hazardous chemical and biological agents in the workplace. Completion of annual university safety training, as appropriate. Applicant should have laboratory experience to include basic laboratory skills and experience working with biological samples. cond_0273.intro: This position is for a Sr. Research Specialist to work in a busy immunology core facility specializing in flow cytometry, cell sorting, and multiplex biomarker assays using Luminex and ELISA. Experience in flow cytometry is desired but not required. After initial training, the successful candidate will work independently or with minimal supervision. Applicants must demonstrate attention to detail, as well as good communication and critical thinking skills. Organization, efficiency, problem solving skills, resourcefulness, and flexibility are required for this position.
cond_0273.responsibilities: Preparation of samples for flow cytometric assays. Support research projects including thawing cryopreserved cells, staining cells with fluorescently labelled antibodies and flow cytometry sample acquisition. Data interpretation, analysis, and data entry. Train students, staff, and faculty to operate flow cytometers. Assist core facility users with flow cytometry experimental design, optimization, and troubleshooting. Discussion of testing results with laboratory manager, laboratory director, and core facility users. Analysis of data, formulation of conclusions, and creation of appropriate statistical presentations, including graphs and charts, for the purpose of reporting research/laboratory results. Using various software applications, such as Microsoft Office, GraphPad Prism, FlowJo and other flow cytometry software programs to analyze, format and present data and/or test reports. Excellent organizational and time management skills required. Independent and self-motivated, requiring limited supervision once trained. Highly organized and detail oriented. Ability to manage multiple and competing priorities required. Excellent oral and written communication skills required. Demonstrated strong, positive interpersonal skills. Ability to communicate effectively and work in a collaborative team environment. Maintenance of laboratory supplies and laboratory equipment. Preparation of standard laboratory solutions, media, and reagents following standard laboratory protocols and procedures. Rigorous use of universal safety precautions to protect self and co-workers from biohazardous materials, including blood-borne pathogens. Compliance with biohazard safety standards through proper handling of potentially hazardous chemical and biological agents in the workplace. Completion of annual university safety training, as appropriate. Applicant should have laboratory experience to include basic laboratory skills and experience working with biological samples. Perform reasonable job duties even if not part of the job description, as assigned by the Principal Investigator or laboratory supervisor.
cond_0273.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Biology, Chemistry, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Around four years of experience in a comparable laboratory performing relevant techniques, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Familiarity with basic laboratory skills and experience working with biological samples.
Preferred Requirements
Experience running flow cytometers and/or setting up flow cytometry assays.
Master's degree with related graduate research (may substitute for experience to the extent permitted by the equivalency formula).
Applicants who do not yet meet the posted requirements but are completing their final academic semester/quarter will be considered eligible for employment and may be asked to provide additional information confirming their academic completion date.

Applicants must demonstrate attention to detail, as well as good communication and critical thinking skills. Organization, efficiency, problem solving skills, resourcefulness, and flexibility are required for this position.
cond_0413.responsibilities:
Prepare samples for flow cytometric assays and lead research project tasks including thawing cryopreserved cells, staining cells with fluorescently labelled antibodies, and executing flow cytometry sample acquisition.
Interpret, analyze, and enter data with accuracy and accountability.
Train students, staff, and faculty to operate flow cytometers.
Direct core facility users in flow cytometry experimental design, optimization, and troubleshooting.
Lead discussions of testing results with the laboratory manager, laboratory director, and core facility users.
Analyze data, formulate conclusions, and produce appropriate statistical presentations, including graphs and charts, for reporting research and laboratory results.
Use software applications such as Microsoft Office, GraphPad Prism, FlowJo, and other flow cytometry programs to analyze, format, and present data and test reports.
Manage multiple and competing priorities with strong organizational and time management skills.
Maintain laboratory supplies and equipment.
Prepare standard laboratory solutions, media, and reagents following established protocols and procedures.
Apply universal safety precautions rigorously to protect self and co-workers from biohazardous materials, including blood-borne pathogens.
Ensure compliance with biohazard safety standards through proper handling of potentially hazardous chemical and biological agents.
Complete annual university safety training as appropriate.
Take on reasonable job duties as assigned by the Principal Investigator or laboratory supervisor, even if outside the standard job description.
cond_0413.requirements:
Bachelor's Degree in Biology, Chemistry, or related field.
Four years of experience in a comparable laboratory performing relevant techniques.
Master's Degree with related graduate research may substitute for experience to the extent permitted by the equivalency formula.
Experience running flow cytometers and/or setting up flow cytometry assays.
Basic laboratory skills and experience working with biological samples.
Applicants who do not meet the posted requirements but are completing their final academic semester/quarter will be considered eligible for employment and may be asked to provide additional information confirming their academic completion date.
The successful candidate will be subject to a pre-employment background check. A prior criminal history does not automatically preclude candidates from employment. The university will review, on an individual basis, the date of a candidate's conviction, the nature of the conviction, and how the conviction relates to an essential job-related qualification or function.
Vaccination requirements apply as mandated. Exceptions may be provided for religious beliefs or medical reasons upon request.
The pre-employment physical for this position requires documentation of immune status against Rubella, Rubeola, Mumps, Varicella, Hepatitis B, and documentation of having received the Tdap vaccination. Any required vaccinations will be provided at no cost through the Occupational Health office.

After initial training, the successful candidate will work independently or with minimal supervision. Applicants must demonstrate attention to detail, as well as good communication and critical thinking skills. Organization, efficiency, problem solving skills, resourcefulness, and flexibility are required for this position. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of flow cytometry workflows and assay design.
cond_0436.responsibilities: Preparation of samples for flow cytometric assays. Support research projects including thawing cryopreserved cells, staining cells with fluorescently labelled antibodies and flow cytometry sample acquisition. Data interpretation, analysis, and data entry. Train students, staff, and faculty to operate flow cytometers. Assist core facility users with flow cytometry experimental design, optimization, and troubleshooting. Discussion of testing results with laboratory manager, laboratory director, and core facility users. Analysis of data, formulation of conclusions, and creation of appropriate statistical presentations, including graphs and charts, for the purpose of reporting research/laboratory results. Using various software applications, such as Microsoft Office, GraphPad Prism, FlowJo and other flow cytometry software programs to analyze, format and present data and/or test reports. Excellent organizational and time management skills required. Independent and self-motivated, requiring limited supervision once trained. Highly organized and detail oriented. Ability to manage multiple and competing priorities required. Excellent oral and written communication skills required. Demonstrated strong, positive interpersonal skills. Ability to communicate effectively and work in a collaborative team environment. Maintenance of laboratory supplies and laboratory equipment. Preparation of standard laboratory solutions, media, and reagents following standard laboratory protocols and procedures. Rigorous use of universal safety precautions to protect self and co-workers from biohazardous materials, including blood-borne pathogens. Compliance with biohazard safety standards through proper handling of potentially hazardous chemical and biological agents in the workplace. Completion of annual university safety training, as appropriate. Applicant should have laboratory experience to include basic laboratory skills and experience working with biological samples. Perform reasonable job duties even if not part of the job description, as assigned by the Principal Investigator or laboratory supervisor.

cond_0438.intro: We are looking for a Sr. Research Specialist to join our team in a busy immunology core facility specializing in flow cytometry, cell sorting, and multiplex biomarker assays using Luminex and ELISA. After initial training, you will work independently or with minimal supervision. The role calls for strong attention to detail, good communication, critical thinking, and the ability to stay organized and flexible in a busy lab setting.
cond_0438.responsibilities:
Prepare samples for flow cytometric assays.
Support research projects including thawing cryopreserved cells, staining cells with fluorescently labelled antibodies, and flow cytometry sample acquisition.
Interpret, analyze, and enter data.
Train students, staff, and faculty to operate flow cytometers, staying in regular contact to answer questions and guide their progress.
Work closely with core facility users on experimental design, optimization, and troubleshooting — actively engaging with them to clarify needs and resolve issues early.
Discuss testing results daily with the laboratory manager, laboratory director, and core facility users.
Analyze data, draw conclusions, and create statistical presentations including graphs and charts for reporting research and laboratory results.
Use software applications such as Microsoft Office, GraphPad Prism, FlowJo, and other flow cytometry programs to analyze, format, and present data and test reports.
Maintain laboratory supplies and equipment.
Prepare standard laboratory solutions, media, and reagents following established protocols.
Apply universal safety precautions consistently to protect yourself and co-workers from biohazardous materials, including blood-borne pathogens.
Handle potentially hazardous chemical and biological agents in compliance with biohazard safety standards.
Complete annual university safety training as appropriate.
Perform reasonable job duties as assigned by the Principal Investigator or laboratory supervisor, even if outside the standard job description.

Applicants must demonstrate attention to detail, as well as good communication and critical thinking skills. cond_0457.responsibilities:
Prepare samples for flow cytometric assays.
Support research projects including thawing cryopreserved cells, staining cells with fluorescently labelled antibodies, and flow cytometry sample acquisition.
Perform data interpretation, analysis, and data entry.
Train students, staff, and faculty to operate flow cytometers.
Assist core facility users with flow cytometry experimental design, optimization, and troubleshooting.
Document and communicate testing results to the laboratory manager, laboratory director, and core facility users as needed.
Analyze data, formulate conclusions, and produce appropriate statistical outputs including graphs and charts for reporting research and laboratory results.
Use software applications such as Microsoft Office, GraphPad Prism, FlowJo, and other flow cytometry programs to analyze, format, and share data and test reports.
Manage multiple priorities with strong organizational and time management skills.
Work independently with limited supervision once trained.
Maintain laboratory supplies and equipment.
Prepare standard laboratory solutions, media, and reagents following established protocols.
Apply universal safety precautions to protect against biohazardous materials, including blood-borne pathogens.
Handle potentially hazardous chemical and biological agents in compliance with biohazard safety standards.
Complete annual university safety training as required.
Perform reasonable job duties as assigned by the Principal Investigator or laboratory supervisor, even if outside the standard job description.

Basic laboratory skills and experience working with biological samples.

Experience running flow cytometers and/or setting up flow cytometry assays.

Experience in flow cytometry is desired but not required. After initial training, the successful candidate will work independently or with minimal supervision. Applicants must demonstrate attention to detail, as well as clear communication and critical thinking skills. Organization, efficiency, problem solving, resourcefulness, and flexibility are required for this position.
cond_0556.responsibilities:
Preparation of samples for flow cytometric assays.
Support research projects including thawing cryopreserved cells, staining cells with fluorescently labelled antibodies, and flow cytometry sample acquisition.
Data interpretation, analysis, and data entry.
Train students, staff, and faculty to operate flow cytometers.
Assist core facility users with flow cytometry experimental design, optimization, and troubleshooting.
Document and communicate testing results to the laboratory manager, laboratory director, and core facility users as needed.
Analyze data, formulate conclusions, and produce appropriate statistical outputs, including graphs and charts, for reporting research and laboratory results.
Use software applications such as Microsoft Office, GraphPad Prism, FlowJo, and other flow cytometry programs to analyze, format, and deliver data and test reports.
Maintain laboratory supplies and equipment.
Prepare standard laboratory solutions, media, and reagents following established protocols and procedures.
Apply universal safety precautions to protect against biohazardous materials, including blood-borne pathogens.
Comply with biohazard safety standards through proper handling of potentially hazardous chemical and biological agents.
Complete annual university safety training as required.
Perform reasonable job duties as assigned by the Principal Investigator or laboratory supervisor, even if outside the standard job description.
cond_0556.requirements:
Bachelor's Degree in Biology, Chemistry, or a related field.
Four years of experience in a comparable laboratory performing relevant techniques.
Master's Degree with related graduate research may substitute for experience to the extent permitted by the equivalency formula.
Experience running flow cytometers and/or setting up flow cytometry assays.
Basic laboratory skills and experience working with biological samples.
Strong organizational and time management skills.
Ability to work independently with limited supervision once trained.
Detail-oriented with the ability to manage multiple competing priorities.
Strong written communication skills and clear, direct verbal reporting.
Ability to coordinate effectively within a team environment.
Pre-employment background check required.
Pre-employment physical with documentation of immune status against specified diseases may be required depending on campus location.
cond_0556.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
cond_0556.inclusion: [Company name masked] is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. We therefore welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics.

cond_0567.intro: This position is for an experienced Sr. Research Specialist to work alongside colleagues in a busy immunology core facility. The facility specializes in flow cytometry, cell sorting, and multiplex biomarker assays using Luminex and ELISA. The successful candidate will work cooperatively with lab staff and core facility users, and should demonstrate attention to detail, good communication, and critical thinking skills. Organization, efficiency, problem solving, resourcefulness, and flexibility are important for this role.
cond_0567.responsibilities:
Prepare samples for flow cytometric assays in coordination with the research team, including thawing cryopreserved cells, staining cells with fluorescently labelled antibodies, and supporting flow cytometry sample acquisition.
Help interpret, analyze, and enter data in collaboration with lab staff.
Work with students, staff, and faculty to train them on operating flow cytometers.
Assist core facility users with flow cytometry experimental design, optimization, and troubleshooting.
Share and discuss testing results with the laboratory manager, laboratory director, and core facility users.
Collaborate on data analysis, formulation of conclusions, and creation of statistical presentations including graphs and charts for reporting research and laboratory results.
Use software applications such as Microsoft Office, GraphPad Prism, FlowJo, and other flow cytometry programs to analyze, format, and present data and test reports in coordination with the team.
Support maintenance of laboratory supplies and equipment.
Prepare standard laboratory solutions, media, and reagents following established protocols and procedures.
Follow rigorous universal safety precautions to protect yourself and co-workers from biohazardous materials, including blood-borne pathogens.
Ensure compliance with biohazard safety standards through proper handling of potentially hazardous chemical and biological agents.
Complete annual university safety training as appropriate.
Contribute to reasonable job duties as assigned by the Principal Investigator or laboratory supervisor, even if outside the standard job description.
cond_0567.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's Degree in Biology, Chemistry, or a related field
Four years of experience in a comparable laboratory performing relevant techniques
Basic laboratory skills and experience working with biological samples
Preferred Requirements
Experience running flow cytometers and/or setting up flow cytometry assays
Master's Degree with related graduate research (may substitute for experience to the extent permitted by the equivalency formula)
Applicants who do not meet the posted requirements but are completing their final academic semester/quarter will be considered eligible for employment and may be asked to provide additional information confirming their academic completion date.

cond_0623.responsibilities: Preparation of samples for flow cytometric assays. Support research projects including thawing cryopreserved cells, staining cells with fluorescently labelled antibodies and flow cytometry sample acquisition. Data interpretation, analysis, and data entry. Train students, staff, and faculty to operate flow cytometers. Assist core facility users with flow cytometry experimental design, optimization, and troubleshooting. Discussion of testing results with laboratory manager, laboratory director, and core facility users. Analysis of data, formulation of conclusions, and creation of appropriate statistical presentations, including graphs and charts, for the purpose of reporting research/laboratory results. Using various software applications, such as Microsoft Office, GraphPad Prism, FlowJo and other flow cytometry software programs to analyze, format and present data and/or test reports. Excellent organizational and time management skills required. Independent and self-motivated, requiring limited supervision once trained. Highly organized and detail oriented. Ability to manage multiple and competing priorities required. Excellent oral and written communication skills required. Demonstrated strong, positive interpersonal skills. Ability to communicate effectively and work in a collaborative team environment. Maintenance of laboratory supplies and laboratory equipment. Preparation of standard laboratory solutions, media, and reagents following standard laboratory protocols and procedures. Rigorous use of universal safety precautions to protect self and co-workers from biohazardous materials, including blood-borne pathogens. Compliance with biohazard safety standards through proper handling of potentially hazardous chemical and biological agents in the workplace. Completion of annual university safety training, as appropriate. Applicant should have laboratory experience to include basic laboratory skills and experience working with biological samples. Perform reasonable job duties even if not part of the job description, as assigned by the Principal Investigator or laboratory supervisor.
cond_0623.requirements: Bachelor's Degree in Biology, Chemistry or related field required; advanced degree strongly preferred. Minimum four years of demonstrated expertise in a comparable laboratory performing relevant techniques. Master's Degree, with related graduate research, may substitute for experience to the extent permitted by the equivalency formula. Proven track record operating flow cytometers and/or setting up flow cytometry assays.
